title: Solar system motion should show sensitive dependence over millions of years

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Solar system motion should show sensitive dependence over millions of years

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although planetary motion looks regular on human timescales, sensitive dependence on initial conditions should ultimately occur in the solar system, producing significant randomness over a few million years that may explain some present-day features of the solar system.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But calculations imply that sensitive dependence on initial conditions should ultimately occur even in our solar system.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “Chaos Theory and Randomness from Initial Conditions” (from p. 304), p. 314. Scope: orbital dynamics of planets and other bodies in the solar system

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern ephemerides and numerical integrators directly test million-year sensitivity and provide adequate initial-state constraints. The explanatory link to particular current features is less decisive, but the central prediction is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Integrate ensembles of high-precision Solar System initial conditions drawn from observational covariance, estimate Lyapunov times and divergence over millions of years, and compare resulting orbital distributions with present dynamical features. Lack of exponential divergence would refute the sensitive-dependence component.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Long integrations require specialist numerical controls.

Chaos does not by itself identify the origin of present-day features.

Rare close encounters amplify model uncertainty.

operationalizability: 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public JPL ephemerides and standard n-body integrations are enough to test whether nearby solar-system trajectories diverge over a few million years, which is the dynamical core of the sentence. That computation is specialist work, and published integrations already exist to audit. The hedge that this may explain some present-day features names nothing that a divergence plot could confirm or refute.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Integrate the planetary equations from public ephemerides with a tiny change in initial conditions and measure divergence over a few million years. Exponential separation supports sensitive dependence on that timescale; bounded separation would challenge it. The clause about present-day features needs a named feature the divergence is supposed to explain.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Significant randomness has no numeric divergence threshold.

May explain some present-day features names no feature.

Million-year integrations mix sensitive dependence with truncation and model error.
